The provost has asked for a year-over-year academic performance comparison between Fall 2013 and Fall 2014. We need to identify courses that were offered in both semesters and compare their enrollment numbers, assignment counts, and average submission scores.

Please query the learning management system data to find courses with course codes ending in "2013J" and "2014J". Match courses that share the same prefix (for example AAA-2013J and AAA-2014J are the same course offered in different years) — only include a course prefix when it exists in both semesters. For each matched pair, compare the enrollment (total_students), the number of assignments, and the average submission score. The average submission score is the mean of all non-null submission scores in the course (i.e. a simple average over every graded submission, not a per-student average).

Create an Excel file called Year_Over_Year_Comparison.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be named "Course Comparison" with columns Course_Name (the common course name without the year suffix), Fall_2013_Enrollment, Fall_2014_Enrollment, Enrollment_Change (2014 minus 2013), Fall_2013_Assignments, Fall_2014_Assignments, Fall_2013_Avg_Grade (rounded to 2 decimal places), Fall_2014_Avg_Grade (rounded to 2 decimal places), and Grade_Change (2014 avg minus 2013 avg, rounded to 2 decimal places). Sort rows alphabetically by Course_Name. The second sheet should be named "Summary" with two columns, Metric and Value, containing these rows: Courses_Compared (number of course pairs), Avg_Enrollment_Change (average of all enrollment changes, rounded to 1 decimal), Avg_Grade_Change (average of all grade changes, rounded to 2 decimal places).

Create a Word document called Academic_Year_Comparison.docx in the workspace. The document should have the title "Fall 2013 vs Fall 2014 Academic Performance Review" followed by a narrative paragraph for each course pair describing the enrollment and grade changes. Conclude with a summary paragraph.

Create a Google Sheet titled "Academic Year Comparison" with a sheet called "Comparison Data" containing the same data as the Excel Course Comparison sheet.

nodes.text:
You are gathering read-only data from a Canvas LMS instance for a provost-level year-over-year comparison between Fall 2013 and Fall 2014. You already know: Canvas is reachable (health check OK, current user Dr. Oliver Murphy, user id 1), the root account is id=1 named "Open University". Do not write any files; just return your results as text.

Task:
1. List all courses in account 1: use canvas_list_account_courses with account_id=1, with_enrollments=true, completed=true. If needed, also do a second call with published=true and merge. Note the total number of courses returned so you can confirm completeness.

2. Filter to courses whose course_code ENDS WITH "2013J" (Fall 2013 cohort) or "2014J" (Fall 2014 cohort). Example course codes look like "AAA-2013J".

3. Pair courses that share the same prefix, where prefix = course_code without the trailing "-2013J"/"-2014J" suffix (e.g. "AAA-2013J" and "AAA-2014J" share prefix "AAA"). Keep ONLY prefixes that exist in BOTH semesters. Report any unpaired courses you excluded.

4. For EVERY matched course instance (both the 2013 and 2014 instance), collect:
   a. Enrollment = total students. Prefer a total_students-style count: if the account course listing (with_enrollments=true) returned an enrollments array with counts, use the student count from there and state how you derived it. Otherwise fall back to canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and count enrollment records whose enrollment_state is "active" or "invited" (page through all results). Be consistent and document which method you used.
   b. Assignment count: call canvas_list_assignments(course_id) and count the assignments.
   c. Average submission score: call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id, per_page=100) with student_ids=["all"], paging until pagination.has_more is false. Collect every submission whose "score" field is non-null (ignore null scores entirely). Compute the simple arithmetic mean of those scores across ALL submissions (not per-student). Keep the result at full precision (report at least 4 decimal places). Also report how many graded submissions and how many null-score submissions were seen per course.

5. Return your final answer as a single compact JSON block (and a short methodology note), shaped exactly like:
{
  "method": {
    "enrollment_source": "<how total_students was derived>",
    "total_courses_in_account": <n>,
    "courses_2013J_found": <n>,
    "courses_2014J_found": <n>,
    "unpaired_courses_excluded": ["<course codes>"]
  },
  "pairs": [
    {
      "prefix": "AAA",
      "course_name_2013": "<full Canvas course name of the 2013 course>",
      "course_name_2014": "<full Canvas course name of the 2014 course>",
      "course_id_2013": <id>,
      "course_id_2014": <id>,
      "course_code_2013": "AAA-2013J",
      "course_code_2014": "AAA-2014J",
      "enrollment_2013": <int>,
      "enrollment_2014": <int>,
      "assignment_count_2013": <int>,
      "assignment_count_2014": <int>,
      "avg_score_2013": <float, 4+ decimals>,
      "avg_score_2014": <float, 4+ decimals>,
      "graded_submissions_2013": <int>,
      "graded_submissions_2014": <int>
    }
  ]
}
Sort "pairs" alphabetically by prefix. If any course has zero graded submissions, set its avg_score to null.

Acceptance criteria: every pair has both enrollment ints, both assignment counts, and both avg scores (or null with an explanation); JSON is valid and compact; no files written.
Gather Canvas YoY course data

Create two local artifacts in the directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-comparison-word/workspace (this path is within your allowed directories). All data is given to you below; do not query any external system.

=== ARTIFACT 1: Excel workbook ===
File: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-canvas-course-comparison-word/workspace/Year_Over_Year_Comparison.xlsx

Sheet 1 — named exactly "Course Comparison". Row 1 is the header (exactly these 9 column names in order):
Course_Name | Fall_2013_Enrollment | Fall_2014_Enrollment | Enrollment_Change | Fall_2013_Assignments | Fall_2014_Assignments | Fall_2013_Avg_Grade | Fall_2014_Avg_Grade | Grade_Change
